title: Ames, Wittich, Mestrezat: define faith by refuge-fiducia fleeing to mercy in Christ
source_text: LXXXV. Alii vero fidem definiunt ab alio actu, scilicet, ab illa fiducia, qua peccator poenitens ad Deum confugit, & Deo adhaeret, eique innititur, ut misericordiam per Christum consequatur. Ita Amesio fides definitur, Acquiescentia cordis in Deo, tanquam in authore vitae, vel salutis aeternae; ut per ipsum ab omni malo liberemur, & omne bonum consequamur. Wittichio, Fames & sitis justitiae, & acquiescentia cordis in Deo, ut fonte & authore salutis; ut ei animas nostras in angustiis & tentationibus committamus. Et Joanni Mestrezatio, Perfugium peccatoris poenitentis ad Dei misericordiam in Christo.
pass_a_gloss: But others define faith from another act, namely from that trust by which the repenting sinner flees to God, and adheres to God, and leans upon him, that he may obtain mercy through Christ. Thus by Ames faith is defined, Rest of the heart in God, as in the author of life, or of eternal salvation; that through him we may be freed from every evil, and obtain every good. By Wittich, Hunger and thirst for righteousness, and rest of the heart in God, as the fountain and author of salvation; that we may commit our souls to him in straits and temptations. And by John Mestrezat, The refuge of the repenting sinner to the mercy of God in Christ.
pass_b_english: Another definitional path: faith = the refuge-fiducia by which the repenting sinner flees to God, adheres, and leans on him for mercy through Christ.
Ames: heart’s rest in God as author of life/eternal salvation — freed from every evil, gaining every good.
Wittich: hunger and thirst for righteousness plus heart-rest in God as salvation’s fountain — committing the soul in straits and temptations.
Mestrezat: the repenting sinner’s refuge to God’s mercy in Christ.
